newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil house says re-election only for same post.
newsitem.headline: Brazil house says re-election only for same post.

text.p: Brazil's lower house approved an amendment to a re-election bill that would force office holders seeking a different public position to step down, officials said.
Under the government-sponsored proposal, if presidents, governors or mayors wished to be elected for different posts, they would have to resign six months before the ballot, the officials said.
The amendment was one of several changes being proposed to a constitutional amendment aproved Tuesday night that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to seek another term.

Earlier, the lower house rejected a proposal to stagger re-election. That change would have made Cardoso elIgible in 1998 but governors and mayors only eligible to stand again in 2002 and 2004 respectively.
Other proposals that must still be voted on include one linking re-election to a plebiscite and another requiring office holders to resign six months before re-election.
